Focus Area: Deploy the fraud model as a TRANSFER-payment review queue
Recommendation: 100% of 4062 suspected-fraud orders used TRANSFER payment (chi2=10882.6, p<0.001) - a model using payment type alone catches 98% of fraud at 8% precision. Route TRANSFER orders through additional verification rather than blocking them outright, given the low precision.

Focus Area: Fix the First Class and Second Class delivery promise, not the logistics
Recommendation: First Class promises 1 day but averages 2 (95% late); Second Class promises 2 but averages 4 (77% late). Standard Class promises 4 and delivers in ~4 (38% late, the best of the four). Re-set the promised delivery windows for the two premium tiers to match actual fulfillment capability - this is a promise-setting fix, not an operations fix.

Focus Area: Investigate the Fitness and Outdoors conversion gap
Recommendation: Fitness draws 16.3% of browse traffic but only 1.4% of orders (0.09x conversion index) - by far the weakest of the six comparable departments. Outdoors is similarly under-converting (0.32x). Audit product pages, pricing, and checkout flow for these two departments specifically.

Focus Area: Replicate Fan Shop's approach in other departments
Recommendation: Fan Shop converts browse traffic into orders at 2.27x its traffic share - the strongest performer by a wide margin. Whatever merchandising or pricing approach it uses is worth testing in Apparel and Golf, which convert well but not as strongly.

Focus Area: Treat the Oct 2017-Jan 2018 sales figures as a data-quality issue, not a business trend
Recommendation: Average order value drops from ~$476 to ~$156 across these four months while order counts rise - investigate the source system for this period before using it in any revenue forecast or year-over-year comparison.
